chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Yahya ibn Musawir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Suweiq (a type of flour soup) strips the bile and phlegm from the stomach with a stripping, and repels seventy types from the types of afflictions.

key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: Suweiq, a traditional dish made from roasted flour, often mixed with water or milk.
key_terms.الْبَلْغَمَ: Phlegm, a viscous secretion in the respiratory system or stomach.
key_terms.الْمِرَّةَ: Bile, specifically referring to the bitter digestive fluid.

ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of Suweiq according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies Suweiq, a simple porridge of wheat flour and water, as a potent prophylactic that clears the stomach of bile and phlegm while warding off seventy distinct types of ailments. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on practical, accessible dietary remedies for maintaining physical purity and preventing disease, reflecting the holistic view of health in the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings.
